clue.text: Enigmatic Study in Scarlet having appeal to English

indicators.note: Study in Scarlet tells us to put the word for study inside the colour word

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
to con is to study or learn by heart
IT is sex appeal, as in the 1920s 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A Sherlock Holmes novel is described as an enigmatic read with English appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Italics make A Study in Scarlet look like the Conan Doyle title, but 'in' is a container signal, and 'having' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite knowledge is obscure and little known, so it is enigmatic or hard to fathom.

clue.text: Cold chamber, by the sound of it

indicators.note: signals that the word for chamber is to be heard rather than spelt as it stands

parts.note: a chamber is a room

explanation.surface: A chilly room seems to be described from what one hears.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is watery discharge from the nose and eyes, an old word for a head cold.

clue.text: Engine part, when running, has to mark emission level

parts.note: carb is short for carburettor, a part of a petrol engine
a machine that is running is on
a footprint is a mark left by a foot

explanation.surface: A component of an engine, while it runs, must record how much it emits.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbon footprint measures the greenhouse gas a person or activity emits, so it is a level of emissions.

clue.text: She will go after teachers in case of compressed information

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain
she will contracts to she'll, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A woman follows the teaching staff in some legal matter involving condensed data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just places the woman's piece behind the teachers. NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutshell is literally the case of a nut, and 'in a nutshell' means information compressed into a few words.

clue.text: Mint rebuilt to accommodate gold supplier now expected

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside
something rebuilt is put together again in a new shape, so the letters of mint are rearranged

parts.note: a mine is where gold comes from

explanation.surface: The Royal Mint is being reconstructed to make room for a gold supplier, as expected now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' turns MINT into IMNT, the anagram the parse does not state, before the gold supplier goes inside after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imminent is about to happen, so it is expected at any moment now.

clue.text: Guarantee unconfident leader's to be changed

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for unconfident is to be swapped for another one

parts.note: someone unconfident is unsure

explanation.surface: A diffident chief must be replaced, it is promised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader's to be changed' swaps the first letter of UNSURE, U, for E.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make certain of it, which is to guarantee it.

clue.text: One's own room aboard makes transport popular

parts.note: a cab is a taxi, a form of transport
something popular is in, or fashionable

explanation.surface: Getting a private room on a ship turns a means of travel into a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is a private room for a passenger on a ship.

clue.text: Arnica might be produced if these are broken

indicators.note: things broken apart are reassembled, so the letters of arnica are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arnica, the bruise remedy, could be made if certain skulls were cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer, broken up, gives ARNICA, so 'these' is the definition and the answer is the anagram of ARNICA.
explanation.definitionFit: The skulls whose breaking would yield arnica are the plural of cranium, which is what 'these' stands for.

clue.text: Brilliant flyers despair if board's reformed

indicators.note: something reformed is made again in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gorgeous birds lose hope when the management board is restructured.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of paradise are tropical birds famous for their brilliant plumage.

clue.text: Its occupants bring together information and opinion

definitions.text: Its occupants bring together information and opinion

parts.note: news is information about recent events
a stand is a position or opinion on an issue

explanation.surface: Newspapers and magazines on sale combine reporting with comment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a newsstand's occupants are its papers, which put news alongside a stand, or editorial opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsstand is a stall selling newspapers, which combine news with opinion.

clue.text: Not speaking about arrival back is a mistake

indicators.note: back says the whole assembly is read from right to left
about means around, so the word for silent goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: someone not speaking is mute
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrival

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about turning up late is an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes MUTARRE, which the parse does not show, and 'back' then turns the whole of it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in printing or writing, so it is a mistake.

clue.text: Robin's slayer used extremely sharp weapon

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word sharp

parts.note: an arrow is a weapon shot from a bow

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's killer used a very keen weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme 'Who Killed Cock Robin?' the sparrow confesses to killing him with his bow and arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the sparrow is the bird who killed Cock Robin, so it is the robin's slayer.

clue.text: Hang around with low companion

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone loiters alongside a lowly friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' reads as humble, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to loiter or wander about aimlessly, which is to hang around.

clue.text: Drug agent has problems out east, making a bloomer

parts.note: narc is US slang for a narcotics agent

indicators.note: out tells us the abbreviation for east leaves the word for problems

parts.note: issues are problems
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A narcotics officer with troubles in the Orient ends up making a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flower. 'out' removes E from ISSUES to leave ISSUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The narcissus is a flowering plant such as the daffodil, so it produces blooms.

clue.text: After bungled action, Heather's keeping quiet

parts.note: a muff is a clumsy failure, as in a muffed catch
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: Heather says nothing after making a mess of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name; it is the plant LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Muffling a sound deadens it, keeping it quiet.

clue.text: Aircraft helping movement of people

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft
a ration is an allotted helping or portion

explanation.surface: Planes are assisting a mass transfer of population.
explanation.definitionFit: Migration is the movement of people or animals from one region to another.

clue.text: Old king's liver failing at last

indicators.note: the word for liver fails, losing its final letter

parts.note: liver is a kind of offal

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch's liver gives out in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for Offa's Dyke on the English and Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia, so he is an old king.

clue.text: Type of money that does grow on trees

definitions.text: Type of money that does grow on trees

parts.words: Type of money that does grow on trees
parts.note: an unexpected sum of money shares its name with fruit blown down from a tree, defying the saying that money does not grow on trees

explanation.surface: Here is a kind of cash that, contrary to the proverb, sprouts from branches.
explanation.definitionFit: A windfall is both an unexpected sum of money and fruit blown off a tree.

clue.text: A run with the spooks can be distressing!

definitions.text: A run with the spooks can be distressing!

parts.note: to lope is to run with a long easy stride
spooks are spies, and the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: Running alongside ghosts can be quite upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressing' is read as removing tresses: alopecia is hair loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Alopecia is baldness or hair loss, which literally takes away one's tresses.

clue.text: Is this show to continue? I don't believe it!

definitions.meaning: to keep going or carry on
an exclamation of disbelief, as in 'get away!'

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a comedy show should carry on, then scoffs in disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is this show' points to The Goon Show, a classic BBC radio comedy, whose title begins with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Go on means carry on, and 'Go on!' is a cry of incredulity.

clue.text: A huge number knocking back drink, including sick one

indicators.note: the reversed drink takes the next pieces inside it
knocking back here means turning the word for drink round, not drinking it

parts.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits
ill means sick
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drinker downing spirits, ill as can be, is a vast figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' looks like drinking but here turns the drink round, giving MARD, which the parse does not show.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliard is an old British name for a thousand million, a huge number.

clue.text: Language spoken in train socially

indicators.note: spoken says the language name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Finnish is the language of Finland

explanation.surface: A tongue is being used during a sociable rail journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway train; it is a verb, as at a finishing school, where young people were taught social graces.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish a young person was to give them social polish, as at a finishing school.

clue.text: Latin is not exactly an upright type

definitions.meaning: the ... languages are the branch of Indo-European that includes Latin
sloping typeface, as opposed to roman upright type

explanation.surface: Latin is said to be a somewhat devious character.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic names the language group including Latin and a sloping style of type.

clue.text: Given a job to make a piano sharp

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
something sharp is pointed

explanation.surface: Someone is hired to tune a piano a shade high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' and 'sharp' suggest music, but P is just the score marking and sharp means pointed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone appointed has been named to a post, so they have been given a job.

clue.text: Stage in which heaps become confused

indicators.note: letters that become confused are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Piles get muddled at a certain point.
explanation.definitionFit: A phase is a stage in a process or development.

clue.text: Chances rugby competition won't start?

indicators.note: the word for the rugby competition loses its opening letter

parts.note: sevens is a form of rugby played seven-a-side in tournaments

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about the odds of a rugby tournament not going ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens are betting odds of one to one, an equal chance of winning or losing.

clue.text: In computer studies I get a beginner to sign off

parts.note: IT is information technology, studied as computing
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A student taking IT gets a novice to approve something.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the L-plates a learner driver must display in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To initial a document is to mark it with one's initials as approval, signing it off.

clue.text: Expert I have employed for historical records

parts.note: arch means chief or master, as in archangel or arch-villain, hence a top expert
I have contracts to I've, with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A specialist says he has been hired to look after old documents.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a collection of historical documents and records.

clue.text: Strange chant, obviously

indicators.note: strange means odd or unusual, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A peculiar song, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: Natch is informal slang short for naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Natch is slang for naturally, used to mean of course or obviously.

clue.text: Artistic assemblies containing new proteins

indicators.note: the artworks word holds the abbreviation for new inside it

parts.note: collages are artworks assembled from pieces stuck together

explanation.surface: Artworks made of scraps include novel proteins.
explanation.definitionFit: Collagens are the structural proteins found in skin, bone and connective tissue.
